question.:question/problem: Which of the following graphs shows the line $y=-2x?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We need to find two distinct points that lie on our line. Any two points will do!

- For the first point, we will let the $x$-coordinate be $x=0.$ Then the $y$-coordinate is 

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-2x \\  & =-2(0) \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the first point is $(0,0).$

- For the second point, we will let the $x$-coordinate be $x=1.$ Then the $y$-coordinate is

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-2x \\  & =-2(1) \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second point is $(1,-2).$

Finally, we plot those two points on the $xy$-plane and draw a line through them. This is the graph of $y=-2x.$ 

![](images/c6/c632cc2770958b5d73f6e143de0b72d19b2099f9f656ff34f273d88acc4f9cb4.png)

question.:question/problem: Which of the following graphs shows the line $y=- \frac{5}{2}x- \frac{7}{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We need to find two distinct points that lie on our line. Any two points will do!

- For the first point, we will let the $x$-coordinate be $x=0.$ Then the $y$-coordinate is

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =- \frac{5}{2}x- \frac{7}{2} \\  & =- \frac{5}{2}(0)- \frac{7}{2} \\  & =0- \frac{7}{2} \\  & =- \frac{7}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the first point is $(0,- \frac{7}{2}).$

- For the second point, we will let the $x$-coordinate be $x=-4.$ Then the $y$-coordinate is

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =- \frac{5}{2}x- \frac{7}{2} \\  & =- \frac{5}{2}(-4)- \frac{7}{2} \\  & =10- \frac{7}{2} \\  & =\frac{13}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second point is $(-4,\frac{13}{2}).$

Finally, we plot those two points on the $xy$-plane and draw a line through them. This is the graph of $y=- \frac{5}{2}x- \frac{7}{2}.$

![](images/a4/a49ce790ccb7e45450f7ebe82a5a4cf3423a7e3cccf15665e286d649d6822471.png)

question.:question/worked-solution:
We need to find two distinct points that lie on our line. Any two points will do!

- For the first point, we will let the $x$-coordinate be $x=0.$ Then the $y$-coordinate is

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{7}{2}+\frac{5}{4}x \\  & =\frac{7}{2}+\frac{5}{4}(0) \\  & =\frac{7}{2}+0 \\  & =\frac{7}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the first point is $(0,\frac{7}{2}).$

- For the second point, we will let the $x$-coordinate be $x=8.$ Then the $y$-coordinate is

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{7}{2}+\frac{5}{4}x \\  & =\frac{7}{2}+\frac{5}{4}(8) \\  & =\frac{7}{2}+10 \\  & =\frac{27}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second point is $(8,\frac{27}{2}).$

Finally, we plot those two points on the $xy$-plane and draw a line through them. This is the graph of $y=\frac{7}{2}+\frac{5}{4}x.$
